extraction.name: CONTEXTUAL
extraction.description: CONTEXTUAL is a novel dataset featuring human-crafted instructions that require context-sensitive reasoning for text-rich images. It evaluates the ability of large multimodal models to jointly reason over text and visual elements within an image, covering eight real-world scenarios: time reading, shopping, navigation, abstract scenes, mobile application usage, web usage, infographics, and miscellaneous natural scenes. The dataset consists of 506 challenging instructions designed to assess fine-grained visual perception, context-sensitive reasoning, and complex reasoning over embedded text and visual cues.
extraction.creator: Rohan Wadhawan, Hritik Bansal, Kai-Wei Chang, Nanyun Peng
extraction.publisher: Proceedings of the 41st International Conference on Machine Learning, Vienna, Austria. PMLR 235, 2024
extraction.citeAs: CONTEXTUAL: Evaluating Context-Sensitive Text-Rich Visual Reasoning in Large Multimodal Models
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was constructed by sourcing images from six different sources: LAION-5B (for Time, Shopping, Navigation, and Abstract categories), Rico Dataset (for Application Usage), Open WebText Initiative (for Web Usage), and annotated test sets from existing VQA datasets (Infographic and Miscellaneous Natural Scenes). Images were filtered using keyword searches and heuristic-based OCR filtering to ensure suitability for annotation. The dataset includes 506 samples, with 100 samples reserved as a validation set and the remaining 406 kept hidden for testing.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Manual Human Curator, Web Scraping, Secondary Data analysis
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Images sourced from LAION-5B, Rico Dataset, Open WebText Initiative, and annotated test sets from existing VQA datasets (InfographicVQA, STVQA, ESTVQA).
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Images were filtered using keyword searches (e.g., 'clothes text' for shopping) and heuristic-based OCR filtering (PaddleOCR) to select images with the highest number of words. Manual filtering was applied to ensure suitability for annotation, particularly for Time, Shopping, Navigation, and Abstract categories.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: The dataset was annotated in three stages: (1) Shortlisting images for instruction-response pair annotation, (2) Dividing authors into two groups for annotation, and (3) Verification by MTurk workers to ensure correctness. Each sample consists of an <image, instruction, response> triplet, with instructions requiring context-sensitive reasoning over text and visual elements. The annotation process ensured adherence to guidelines and filtered out low-quality samples.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Amazon Mechanical Turk (MTurk) for verification and human performance baseline collection.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: 96% of the samples were annotated correctly during verification. The dataset includes 506 instances after filtering out incorrect samples, with human annotators ensuring adherence to guidelines.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Human annotators were primarily from the US, with qualifications tested before participation. The dataset includes human performance baselines and human evaluations of model responses.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: PaddleOCR for OCR extraction, PP-OCRv4 for OCR extraction, LATIN prompt for layout-aware OCR, ShareGPT-4V-7B for image captions, and GPT-4/GPT-4V for automatic evaluation and synthetic data generation.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset and code are available on Hugging Face and GitHub, with a continuously updated leaderboard on HuggingFace. The dataset includes a validation set of 100 samples, with the remaining 406 samples kept hidden for testing. The dataset is designed for benchmarking and evaluating large multimodal models.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset does not explicitly mention the collection of sensitive human attributes. However, it includes images of real-world scenarios, which may inadvertently capture sensitive information such as personal details in natural scenes or infographics.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset aims to evaluate context-sensitive text-rich visual reasoning in large multimodal models, which have real-world applications such as assisting the visually impaired in navigating public spaces or understanding abstract text-rich images like memes. The dataset ensures that images, instructions, and responses are not offensive to any social group, though it acknowledges the potential for harmful responses from existing multimodal models.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset may inherit biases from the source datasets (e.g., LAION-5B, Rico Dataset) and the human annotation process. For example, the dataset includes images from specific categories (e.g., shopping, navigation) that may reflect cultural or regional biases. The human performance baseline is primarily based on annotators from the US, which may not represent global linguistic diversity.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset is limited to 506 samples, which may not cover all possible real-world scenarios. The dataset focuses on context-sensitive text-rich visual reasoning, which may not generalize to other types of visual reasoning tasks. The dataset includes a validation set of 100 samples, with the remaining 406 samples kept hidden for testing, which may limit the diversity of evaluation scenarios.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, Validation, Fine Tuning. The dataset is designed to benchmark the performance of large multimodal models on context-sensitive text-rich visual reasoning tasks. It provides a framework for evaluating the joint reasoning capabilities of models over embedded text and visual elements in images. The dataset includes human performance baselines and model evaluations, making it suitable for research and development in multimodal AI.
